snapshot: acquisition-order rows [id,x,y,z,time,clearance,line_id,station_id,channel values in sorted channel order]
binding.numbers: All numeric fields/readings become lowercase 16-digit big-endian IEEE-754 float64 hexadecimal strings; null stays null and -0 canonicalizes to +0. Values up to +/-1e100 are supported; Python integer values must be exactly representable as binary64 to prevent lossy hashing. Snapshot is compact UTF-8 JSON arrays (Unicode scalars, ensure_ascii=false), then SHA-256. Metadata/extensions are not included.
binding.runtime: Python hashlib; JS async Web Crypto SHA-256 (Node 20+ or secure browser context).

assumptions: History defaults to unknown. Evidence-backed declarations resolve unknown states; known applied/unapplied states cannot be changed to a different state through these APIs. Registered aliases import legacy global correction declarations conservatively for applicable channels.

Ledger events validate IDs, binding-chain continuity and per-channel state transitions. Applying requires unapplied history and complete support. Reused event IDs, repeated applications, conflicting legacy aliases and stale dataset bindings are rejected. This is a workflow/provenance guard, not authentication against stripped or maliciously rewritten metadata. Retained processing that records a base correction prevents reinitializing a missing ledger.

Base variation is linear_interpolated_base - explicit_reference and corrected = observed - variation. Selected survey magnetic total field/anomaly and stationary base total field must be in nT. This does not remove IGRF, change field type or infer calibration.

UTC Unix seconds and explicit synchronized clock policy are required. Base acquisition times must increase strictly. Null base readings break interpolation; no extrapolation or interpolation across excessive gaps. Exact valid base samples remain usable. Both selected survey and base stream require known unapplied diurnal history; existing base ledgers must validate.

Every nonnull selected survey reading must have supported time coverage before any output/ledger application is committed. Missing survey readings stay null, with original record order and other fields preserved. Unsupported runs return needs_input and proposals but no corrected observations.

Base station IDs must agree; available base XYZ positions must be stationary. The library cannot establish geographic suitability, disturbance-free recording, clock synchronization or calibration truth; caller evidence/QC is required.

Bindings cover normalized data identities/order, geometry/time/clearance, channel definitions and readings, not arbitrary metadata/extensions. Editing data invalidates the ledger. Finite binary64 values up to +/-1e100 are supported. Python integers must be exactly representable; JS numbers already use binary64.

Existing field units, correction declarations and source history are preserved; legacy aggregate states remain synchronized with per-channel states. Numeric changes move uncertainty into flat input lineage and mark uncertainty_propagated=false. No calibrated uncertainty is calculated. Raster workflow v1 is unchanged.

IGRF application events carry the fixed IGRF14 model/coefficient/convention identity and removal parameters. Python executes the optional backend; both runtimes validate/replay the ledger. Retained remove_igrf processing prevents initializing a replacement ledger. See describe_igrf / describeGeophysicsIgrf for execution requirements.

Lag correction uses corrected(t)=input(t+lag_seconds), on unchanged navigation XYZ/time. Positive lag advances delayed magnetic readings. A calibrated constant time lag is supplied explicitly, not inferred from flight speed or sensor geometry. Normally apply lag before time/location-dependent corrections; existing processing stages are preserved as supplied, never inverted or reordered.

Lag interpolation uses only the original selected channel within each acquisition-contiguous line_id segment, including repeated line IDs as separate segments. All records need line_id and strictly increasing UTC times within each segment, including null-reading gap markers. No extrapolation, cross-line interpolation, bridging null source readings or excessive gaps. Existing target nulls stay null.

Lag unsupported_policy=reject returns needs_input and proposals without committing observations. Explicit mask sets unsupported nonnull readings to null and persists their original IDs/values in masked_records; at least one selected reading must be supported. No records or other channels are dropped. Application affected_records counts nonnull readings immediately BEFORE the application. Validators reconstruct historical counts backwards across lag masks, so earlier base/IGRF ledger applications remain valid.

Lag is bounded to 4096 records and +/-3600 seconds. It requires known unapplied per-channel magnetic_lag history, nT total-field/anomaly data, explicit synchronized clock policy, gap limit and calibration evidence. Source metadata/uncertainty moves into standard remappable lineage; no uncertainty propagation is claimed.

Heading correction subtracts an explicitly supplied scalar bias: corrected=observed-bias(heading), with bias_convention=observed_minus_reference. Calibration is copied and sorted, with 2..72 unique heading_degrees in [0,360) and bias_nT. Recorded headings are [0,360], where 360 evaluates as 0. No negative yaw conversion, trajectory-heading inference, calibration fitting or north-reference conversion is performed.

metadata.heading declares key, units=degrees, reference=true_north|magnetic_north|grid_north, positive=clockwise. It must match heading_key/reference options. Heading values come from record.extra[heading_key]; any supplied nonnull value must be a valid angle. Missing headings on missing magnetic readings are allowed. Each nonnull selected reading needs supported heading before an atomic application is committed.

Circular piecewise-linear calibration includes the north seam. Exact nodes remain supported independent of neighbouring gaps; interpolation requires an angular bracket no wider than explicit max_heading_gap (0<gap<=180). Missing headings/context or inadequate angular coverage returns needs_input and proposals but no observations or application event. No heading masks or extrapolation are provided.

Heading execution is bounded to 4096 records. Selected nT total-field/anomaly type, other channels, null readings, geometry/time, order and extras are retained. Known unapplied per-channel magnetic_heading history, unique event ID, calibration_id and evidence are required. Heading/calibration bindings detect accidental edits even after later lag masking; history is a provenance guard, not authentication against deliberate rewriting.

Calibrated heading bias applies only under the instrument/configuration/reference conditions verified by caller evidence. This scalar model does not compensate attitude, manoeuvres, eddy currents or geographic/temporal variation. No calibration parameter estimation, operation reordering or uncertainty propagation is claimed; original uncertainty remains in remappable source lineage.

Fixed-reference levelling holds caller-designated reference lines at zero bias and fits each target with the equally weighted mean target-minus-reference crossover residual. One constant DC bias applies to every nonnull reading on a target, including beyond tie locations. This is an empirical fixed-reference strategy, not global network levelling, polynomial drift, outlier removal, microlevelling or geological interpretation.

Every line must be explicitly classified reference/target. All targets must satisfy min_crossovers, min_reference_lines, max_abs_correction and max_rms_residual before one atomic magnetic_levelling event. Missing readings stay null; geometry/time, field type, order/extras/other channels remain. Native model/context binding supplements the existing observation binding. References/evidence and source corrections must be independently verified; no operation reordering or calibrated uncertainty propagation.

Explicit reprojection events link unchanged correction states across horizontal frames. Earlier events remain unchanged; historical levelling bindings use the original horizontal context. Unsupported readers must reject the extension.

gravity_normal applications retain fixed Boule/model identity, semantic parameters and gravity/height/tide context binding; historical geographic context replays across later supported horizontal reprojections. Output is gravity_disturbance, not a fully reduced anomaly.

snapshot: all acquisition-order [record ID,raw heading float64 hex or null]
heading_binding.numbers: Big-endian 16-digit IEEE-754 float64 hexadecimal, signed zero canonicalized to +0. Compact UTF-8 JSON array then SHA-256. Absent and null headings bind as null; 360 and 0 raw headings bind distinctly. All supplied headings must be [0,360] finite numbers, even on missing magnetic readings. Model nodes canonicalize in ascending angle order. Metadata/context and semantic parameters are bound alongside extra heading inputs. This supplements, and does not change, the general observation binding.

snapshot: canonical horizontal unit and optional [height unit,datum,z_positive]
levelling_binding.numbers: Big-endian 16-digit IEEE-754 float64 hex, signed zero normalized. Compact UTF-8 JSON arrays then SHA-256. Model roles, zero references, finite bounded offsets and current context validate at replay. Original observation binding already protects geometry/line IDs/readings; fit is not recomputed against changed values. Later lag masks use historical pre-event counts.
